items.title: Starbucks Weighs $3.1 Billion Sale of Japan Business
items.summary: The coffee chain reportedly hires Citigroup and Morgan Stanley to evaluate options for its approximately 2,000 Japanese stores.

items.title: Starbucks weighs sale of Japan business worth several billion dollars - Bloomberg
items.summary: Investing.com-- Starbucks Corporation (NASDAQ:SBUX) has hired advisers including Citigroup (NYSE:C) and Morgan Stanley (NYSE:MS) to explore a potential sale of its Japan business, which could be valued at several billion dollars, Bloomberg News reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter.

items.title: Starbucks Is Said to Engage Banks for Sale of Japan Business
items.summary: Starbucks Corp. has tapped advisers to prepare for a potential sale of its Japan business for several billion dollars, according to people familiar with the matter.

items.title: Who is holding Jensen Huang accountable? It sure looks like nobody
items.summary: Sozzi Unleashed host Brian Sozzi digs into day two of Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia. Including a Financial Times report that interim CEO Colette Kress was left out of the talks to bring Huang back, a Wall Street Journal report that Huang disclosed more affairs to the board than previously known, why Brian says Nvidia is effectively a "board of one," and what history says about returning founders from Steve Jobs and Howard Schultz to Kevin Plank.

items.title: Nvidia stock in focus: Why CEO comebacks are usually good for shares
items.summary: After Nvidia (NVDA) stock surged 31% following news of Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO, Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi takes a closer look at what CEO comebacks have historically done for their respective stocks.
